title: Solar and Battery Rebates in Fort St. John 2026: Up to $10,000
desc: Fort St. John solar and battery rebates for 2026. About 3.31 peak sun hours a day, 50% detached homes. Up to $5,000 for solar and $5,000 for a battery with Peak Saver.
h1: Solar and Battery Rebates in Fort St. John
lead: BC Hydro pays up to $5,000 for solar panels and up to $5,000 for a home battery in Fort St. John. A battery can keep your lights and fridge on in an outage; the rebate makes it cheaper.
cards_heading: What solar and battery rebates pay in Fort St. John
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's solar and battery rebate page on October 3, 2026. The battery rebate is higher if you enroll it in Peak Saver. Every rebate is capped at 50% of what you paid.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW of DC capacity, up to 50% of the installed cost.

cards.title: Battery with Peak Saver
cards.note: $500 per kWh, up to 50% of cost. Enroll in Peak Saver within 14 days of the in-service date. Battery-only allowed.

cards.title: Peak Saver battery reward
cards.note: One-time bill credit for enrolling, then a seasonal reward each winter you stay in.

cards.title: Tesla Powerwall
cards.note: Tesla batteries, inverters and chargers are not eligible for BC Hydro or CleanBC rebates.

sections: How much sun Fort St. John gets

Fort St. John averaged about 3.31 peak sun hours a day from 2020 to 2024. Long summer days make up for very short winter ones, so almost all the output comes from April to September. Snow on the panels also stops output in winter. As a rough guide, a 5 kW system here would make about 4,833 kWh a year, using 3.31 sun hours times 365 days and assuming 80% of the panel rating reaches your panel after losses. Your installer's design for your own roof will be more accurate.

The 2021 Census counted 8,775 households in Fort St. John. 50% of Fort St. John households live in a detached house (4,375 homes), and about 58% own. With cold winters, a battery's backup value during a winter outage is real, but the battery must be installed somewhere it can stay warm enough to work.

Fort St. John's average January low was -15.0°C from 2015 to 2024, and the coldest reading was -42.2°C. Most home batteries have a minimum operating temperature, so where the battery sits matters more here than on the coast. Ask the installer for the model's cold limit and whether it needs a heated space. Winter outages in deep cold are when a battery is worth the most.

A battery stores power for when the grid goes down. The rebate is $500 per kWh, so a 10 kWh battery that cost at least $10,000 can reach $5,000 with Peak Saver. Without Peak Saver, the battery must be paired with solar and the rebate stops at $1,500.
The 50% cap and the order of steps

Every rebate is limited to 50% of the installed cost. You must hire a contractor in the Home Performance Contractor Network and submit a self-generation application to BC Hydro before you install. Wait for technical acceptance. After install, send the final inspection documents and paid invoices. BC Hydro pays within 60 days of approval.
Tesla's Powerwall 2 and 3, Tesla inverters and Tesla chargers are not eligible for BC Hydro or CleanBC rebates. The only exception is an application made before March 12, 2025.

claim_steps: Confirm your home is on BC Hydro's grid.
Hire a Home Performance Contractor Network member.
Submit the self-generation application before you install, and wait for technical acceptance.
Install. Enroll the battery in Peak Saver within 14 days of the in-service date if you want the $5,000 battery rebate.
Send the final inspection documents and paid invoices.
faq: Does solar work in Fort St. John winters?
Very little power comes in December and January. Most comes from April to September.
What does Peak Saver ask of my battery?
BC Hydro can draw on it during a few winter peak events, November to March, for up to four hours. You can opt out of events, but opting out of more than half may cost you the seasonal reward.
Can I get the battery rebate without solar?
Yes, but only if you enroll the battery in Peak Saver. Then the battery-only rebate can reach $5,000.
No. Tesla batteries get $0 from BC Hydro and CleanBC.
Owners of single-family homes, duplexes, townhomes and mobile homes connected to BC Hydro's grid.
